compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`pai_retry.wire_history_processor` is the only place rebar checks a request against a model's
context window before it goes out, and it structurally cannot catch the case that actually
bites: an oversized FIRST request.

`_make_wire_projection`'s `proc(messages)` walks the history and only inspects messages that
are `ModelResponse` AND `_is_failed_output_response` — i.e. a prior text-only turn being
carried onto a RETRY wire. The initial system prompt + user instructions are never measured.
`ContextWindowExceededError` is therefore raised only when a CARRIED response would overflow;
a first request that is already three times the window is handed straight to the provider,
which rejects it with a 400.

That is what happened in bug `569c-931f-69a2-4c1d` (spongy-illjudged-terrier): `enrich()`
sent 2,992,643 characters at a 200,000-token model and got
`'prompt is too long: 206826 tokens > 200000 maximum'`. That bug was fixed **op-locally** —
`enrich()` now bounds its own source — but the seam-level gap remains, and every other op
that assembles input from unbounded store content is exposed to the same failure with no
shared guard.

## Why this matters

The per-op bounds that exist today are independent and inconsistent: `spec_scan` caps each
epic description at `_DESC_CAP`, `plan_review` budgets via `sizing.largest_window_tokens` /
`det_floor`, `workflow/completion` uses `physical_context_ceiling` + `fit_within_ceiling`,
and `enrich` now has its own. A new op gets no protection by default, and the failure mode is
a provider 400 rather than a rebar-typed error an operation can reason about.

## Scope (to be confirmed by whoever claims this)
- `src/rebar/llm/pai_retry.py` — measure the outgoing request's authoritative input against
  the smallest viable candidate window BEFORE the first call, not only when projecting a
  carried retry response.
- Decide the posture per op class: fail closed with `ContextWindowExceededError` (correct for
  verification ops, per the module's stated position) versus delegating to an op-supplied
  bound (correct for lossy summarizer input like the ticket digest). A one-size posture is
  probably wrong; the seam may need to raise a typed error the op can choose to catch.
- Consider whether the existing per-op bounds should then defer to the shared seam.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A first request whose authoritative input alone exceeds the resolved model's window
      raises a rebar-typed error before the provider call, rather than surfacing as a
      provider 400 wrapped in `LLMUnavailableError`.
- [ ] A test drives the oversized-first-request path and observes the typed error (the
      existing `test_rp01_s2_bounded_op_oracle.py` covers only the carried-response case).
- [ ] Ops with a legitimate lossy bound (ticket-digest enrichment) keep working — the seam
      must not turn their now-successful truncated calls back into hard failures.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and CI's pytest invocation are green.

## Provenance
Found while debugging `569c-931f-69a2-4c1d`. Filed rather than folded in: that bug's fix is a
correct op-local bound with runtime-verified results, while this is a change to a shared seam
with cross-op blast radius and a real design question about posture.
compiled_state.title: context-window check never sees the FIRST request
